root_causes.description: The frontend container was forcibly killed ('Killing: Stopping container frontend') and replaced by a newly scheduled pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8. Because the pod was replaced rather than restarted in place, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total stayed at 0, hiding the crash from restart-based alerting. The hard kill produced no error spans or error logs, and the load-generator's retries caused a request-rate burst (max 604.8 req/s vs p50 8.0 req/s) at the start of the window while frontend was unavailable.

evidence.observed_value: get_pod_events(namespace=otel-demo, pod_name_prefix=frontend, since_seconds=1200) returned 'Killing: Stopping container frontend' (count=1) followed by Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started events for replacement pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8
evidence.expected_baseline: No container Killing events; frontend pod runs continuously without replacement

evidence.observed_value: pod_restarts mean=0.000, p50=0.000, p95=0.000, p99=0.000, max=0.000 across the entire window despite the container kill
evidence.expected_baseline: 0 restarts in steady state; the kill manifested as pod replacement (new pod name frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8), so the per-pod restart counter never incremented

evidence.observed_value: request_rate mean=148.190, p50=8.009, p95=432.873, p99=570.433, max=604.823 req/s with anomaly detected at 2026-09-16T08:14:49 (window start)
evidence.expected_baseline: steady request_rate ~8 req/s (p50) consistent with normal load-generator traffic

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.006, p50=0.000, p95=0.019, p99=0.019, max=0.019 — no error spike; search_traces(service_name=frontend, error_only=True) returned no error traces and query_loki {service_name="frontend"} |= "error" returned no logs
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; a hard container kill emits no in-flight error responses, unlike http_abort faults

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis that the container was OOM-killed due to memory pressure. Ruled out: frontend working-set memory remained flat (~253MB mean, ~296MB max) with no pre-kill climb, and the K8s event shows a plain 'Killing' termination with no OOMKilled reason.

evidence.expected_baseline: stable ~250MB working set; an OOM kill would be preceded by a memory climb toward the container limit

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis that a downstream dependency (checkout, cart, payment, product-catalog) failed and propagated errors to frontend. Ruled out: all downstream services showed near-zero error rates during the window and frontend's own error rate never spiked.

evidence.observed_value: checkout error_rate mean=0.004, p50=0.000, p95=0.019, max=0.019; cart, payment, and product-catalog error_rate all 0.000 across the window

remediation_steps: Run kubectl describe pod on the terminated frontend pod and the replacement frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 to capture the termination reason, exit code, and who issued the kill (SIGTERM sender, kubelet, or chaos-injection tooling).
Check Kubernetes audit logs and any chaos-engineering frameworks (e.g., Litmus/pod-kill experiments) active in the cluster to determine whether the kill was injected or operator-initiated.
Scale frontend to at least 2 replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget so a single pod kill does not take the entire frontend tier offline.

Add alerting on pod replacement/termination events (Killing events, kube_pod_container_status_terminated) rather than only restart counters, since this crash registered 0 restarts due to pod replacement.
Configure retry backoff/jitter on the load-generator (and any client retry logic) to prevent the retry storm that drove request_rate from a p50 of 8 req/s to 604 req/s while frontend was unavailable.
